title: 741 comparator — LED on when it gets hot

steps.title: The chip
steps.circuit: Start with the chip. Draw the op-amp triangle and number the pins you will use: 2 (− input), 3 (+ input), 6 (output), 7 and 4 (supply).

steps.title: Supply rails and supply pins
steps.circuit: Draw +9 V along the top and 0 V along the bottom. Pin 7 goes to +9 V and pin 4 to 0 V. Pins 1, 5 and 8 are not used.

steps.title: The sensing divider: TH1 and VR1 → pin 3
steps.circuit: TH1 on top, VR1 below. Their middle point is V<sub>in</sub>, into the + input (pin 3). When TH1 warms up its resistance falls, so V<sub>in</sub> rises. VR1 sets how hot.

steps.title: The reference divider: R2 and R3 → pin 2
steps.circuit: R2 on top, R3 below. Their middle point is V<sub>ref</sub>, about 1.6 V, into the − input (pin 2).

steps.title: The LED
steps.circuit: From pin 6, R4 and the LED go to 0 V. When V<sub>in</sub> is bigger than V<sub>ref</sub>, pin 6 goes HIGH and the LED lights.

steps.title: Test points
steps.circuit: T1 +9 V, T2 0 V, T3 V<sub>in</sub> (pin 3), T4 V<sub>ref</sub> (pin 2), T5 V<sub>out</sub> (pin 6).

quiz.q: On the diagram, V<sub>in</sub> (net 3) goes to the + input. Which 741 pin is that?
o: Pin 3
Right. Pin 3 is the non-inverting (+) input; pin 2 is the inverting (−) input.
Pin 2
Pin 2 is the inverting (−) input, where V<sub>ref</sub> goes. Check the pin-out.
Pin 6
Pin 6 is the output. The + input is pin 3.
Pin 7
Pin 7 is the +9 V supply. The + input is pin 3.

quiz.q: TH1 warms up. What happens to V<sub>in</sub> at pin 3?
o: It rises
Right. TH1's resistance falls, so TH1 takes a smaller share of the 9 V and VR1 a bigger share. V<sub>in</sub> is the voltage across VR1.
It falls
That happens when the thermistor is at the bottom. Here TH1 is on top: as its resistance falls, VR1's share grows.
It stays the same
V<sub>in</sub> depends on how the 9 V is shared between TH1 and VR1. What happens to TH1's resistance when it warms?
It drops to 0 V
VR1 still has a share of the supply. Think about which resistor gets the bigger share as TH1's resistance falls.

quiz.q: When does the LED come on?
o: When V<sub>in</sub> is bigger than V<sub>ref</sub>
Right. The + input (pin 3) is then higher than the − input (pin 2), so the output, pin 6, goes HIGH.
When V<sub>ref</sub> is bigger than V<sub>in</sub>
That makes the output LOW. The comparator's output is HIGH when the + input is the higher one.
When V<sub>in</sub> reaches 9 V
V<sub>in</sub> only has to pass V<sub>ref</sub>, about 1.6 V. Compare the two inputs.
Whenever the supply is on
The output depends on which input is higher. Compare V<sub>in</sub> and V<sub>ref</sub>.
